scope: Selected primary studies supporting seven clinic pathways. Not a systematic review, complete guideline comparison, or clinician signoff.

records.label: ValUE · 2012

source.title: A Randomized Trial of Urodynamic Testing before Stress-Incontinence Surgery

records.population: Women with uncomplicated, demonstrable stress-predominant incontinence.
records.comparison: Office evaluation plus urodynamics vs office evaluation alone

endpoints.name: Composite success: ≥70% UDI improvement and much/very much better on PGI-I
endpoints.result: 76.9% with urodynamics vs 77.2% with office evaluation alone.
endpoints.uncertainty: Difference −0.3 percentage points; 95% CI −7.5 to 6.9. Prespecified noninferiority margin: 11 percentage points.

limitations: Restricted to uncomplicated demonstrable SUI; does not address unclear diagnoses, substantial voiding dysfunction or complex repeat surgery.
records.applicability: Supports omitting routine preoperative urodynamics in appropriately selected index patients.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: TOMUS · 2010

source.title: Retropubic versus Transobturator Midurethral Slings for Stress Incontinence

records.population: Women having surgery for stress urinary incontinence.

endpoints.name: Objective success: negative stress/pad tests and no retreatment
endpoints.uncertainty: Difference 3.0 percentage points; 95% CI −3.6 to 9.6; met the ±12-point equivalence margin.

endpoints.name: Subjective success: no symptoms/diary leakage or retreatment
endpoints.uncertainty: Difference 6.4 percentage points; 95% CI −1.6 to 14.3; did not meet equivalence.

limitations: Voiding dysfunction requiring surgery: 2.7% vs 0%; neurologic symptoms: 4.0% vs 9.4%.
Different endpoints produce different success rates; these are not lifelong cure rates or comparisons with mini-slings.
records.applicability: Discuss endpoint definitions and route-specific complications; no single route is best for every patient.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: OPUS · 2012

source.title: A Midurethral Sling to Reduce Incontinence after Vaginal Prolapse Repair

records.population: Women without symptomatic SUI, with anterior prolapse stage ≥2, undergoing vaginal prolapse repair.
records.comparison: Concomitant midurethral sling vs sham incisions

endpoints.name: Urinary incontinence, allowing subsequent treatment
endpoints.result: 27.3% with sling vs 43.0% without sling; number needed to treat 6.3.

limitations: Sling increased bladder perforation (6.7% vs 0%), UTI (31.0% vs 18.3%) and incomplete emptying at 6 weeks (3.7% vs 0%).
Vaginal-repair population; do not extrapolate directly to abdominal sacrocolpopexy.
records.applicability: Counsel about staged versus concomitant continence surgery using both prevention benefit and procedure-related harms.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: SAVE-U · 10 years

source.title: Sacrospinous Hysteropexy Versus Vaginal Hysterectomy in Women with Uterine Prolapse: 10-year Follow-up of a Randomised Controlled Trial

records.design: Long-term follow-up of a randomized trial
records.population: Women with uterine descent stage ≥2; native-tissue sacrospinous hysteropexy.

sampleSize.analysis: Primary 10-year outcome available in 93 women: 44 hysteropexy and 49 hysterectomy; 89 underwent examination. Earlier failures were incorporated.

records.comparison: Native-tissue sacrospinous hysteropexy vs vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral suspension

endpoints.name: Apical stage ≥2 plus bothersome bulge or repeat apical surgery
endpoints.uncertainty: Difference −6.6 percentage points; 95% CI −19.9 to 6.7; no statistically significant difference.

limitations: Fewer than half of the original randomized participants contributed the 10-year primary endpoint; wide intervals do not establish equivalence.
Published main text and all three tables read; the actual flow-diagram image and supplemental document remain unavailable for this check.
records.applicability: Provides native-tissue uterine-preservation counselling; do not combine its rates with the mesh-based SUPeR trial.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: SUPeR · 10 years

source.title: Sacrospinous Hysteropexy With Mesh vs Vaginal Hysterectomy for Treatment of Uterovaginal Prolapse: 10-Year Results of a Randomized Clinical Trial

records.design: Extended follow-up of a randomized trial
records.population: Postmenopausal women with symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse at 9 US centres.

sampleSize.analysis: 175 eligible for intention-to-treat analysis (88 vs 87); 112 (64%) entered years 6–10 follow-up.

records.comparison: Sacrospinous hysteropexy with vaginal mesh vs vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral suspension

endpoints.name: Composite prolapse beyond hymen, symptoms or retreatment

records.followUp: 10 years; first online June 24, 2026 (August issue date)
limitations: Substantial attrition and loss of masking in years 6–10; no patient-reported outcome difference.
The vaginal mesh product is not currently marketed in the US.
records.applicability: Historical mesh-assisted comparison; not evidence for native-tissue hysteropexy or a recommendation to use unavailable vaginal mesh.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: MASTER · 2021

source.title: Outcomes of a Noninferiority Randomised Controlled Trial of Surgery for Men with Urodynamic Stress Incontinence After Prostate Surgery (MASTER)

records.population: Men with bothersome urodynamic stress incontinence after prostate surgery at 27 UK centres.

sampleSize.analysis: 190 randomized per group; primary responses from 154 sling and 158 AUS participants.

records.comparison: Transobturator male sling vs artificial urinary sphincter (AUS)

endpoints.name: Any patient-reported leakage (strict continence definition)
endpoints.result: Still incontinent: 134/154 (87.0%) with sling vs 133/158 (84.2%) with AUS. Both groups improved symptom scores.
endpoints.uncertainty: Noninferiority established against a 15-percentage-point margin (P=.003); this is not proof of equivalent dryness.

endpoints.name: ICIQ-UI symptom score
endpoints.result: 8.7 with sling vs 7.5 with AUS (lower is better).
endpoints.uncertainty: Adjusted mean difference 1.4; 95% CI 0.2–2.6; statistically different secondary outcomes favoured AUS.

limitations: No blinding; incomplete primary questionnaire response; broad noninferiority margin.
Any leakage differs from social continence or patient satisfaction; do not call 87% a treatment failure rate.
records.applicability: Both can improve symptoms. Select using severity, radiation history, urethral status and ability to operate an AUS.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: MTOPS · 2003

source.title: The Long-Term Effect of Doxazosin, Finasteride, and Combination Therapy on the Clinical Progression of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

records.population: Men ≥50 years with symptomatic BPH and reduced urinary flow.

sampleSize.analysis: Four groups: placebo, doxazosin, finasteride, combination.

records.comparison: Doxazosin, finasteride or combination vs placebo

endpoints.name: Clinical progression: symptom worsening, retention, incontinence, renal insufficiency or recurrent UTI
endpoints.result: Events per 100 person-years: placebo 4.5; doxazosin 2.7; finasteride 2.9; combination 1.5. Combination reduced relative risk by 66%.
endpoints.uncertainty: P<.001 for combination vs placebo; confidence interval not extracted from inspected results.

limitations: Most progression events were symptom-score worsening; the 66% reduction is not a 66% reduction in surgery or an absolute risk difference.
Trial used specific drugs and enrolment criteria; consider prostate enlargement and individual progression risk.
records.applicability: Supports combination therapy for appropriately selected men at risk of progression.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: UPSTREAM · 2020

source.title: Diagnostic Assessment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Men Considering Prostate Surgery: A Noninferiority Randomised Controlled Trial of Urodynamics in 26 Hospitals

records.population: Men with bothersome LUTS in whom prostate surgery was an option.
records.comparison: Routine care plus urodynamics vs routine care alone

endpoints.name: International Prostate Symptom Score
endpoints.result: 12.6 with urodynamics vs 13.1 with routine care.
endpoints.uncertainty: Adjusted difference −0.33; 95% CI −1.47 to 0.80; noninferiority margin 1 point.

endpoints.name: Underwent surgery
endpoints.uncertainty: Adjusted odds ratio 1.05; 95% CI 0.77–1.43; no reduction in surgery.

limitations: Excluded catheter-dependent men, relevant neurological disease and prior prostate surgery.
A pathway trial does not establish that pressure-flow testing is never useful.
records.applicability: Reserve invasive urodynamics for diagnostic uncertainty or situations in which the result can change counselling or treatment.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: OPEN · 2020

source.title: Surgical Treatment for Recurrent Bulbar Urethral Stricture: A Randomised Open-label Superiority Trial of Open Urethroplasty Versus Endoscopic Urethrotomy (The OPEN Trial)

records.population: Men with recurrent bulbar stricture after at least one prior intervention.

sampleSize.analysis: 109 assigned urethroplasty and 113 urethrotomy; incomplete repeated symptom measurements limit the primary analysis.

endpoints.name: Repeated patient-reported voiding symptom score
endpoints.uncertainty: Mean difference −0.36; 95% CI −1.74 to 1.02; no superiority on the primary symptom endpoint.

endpoints.name: Reintervention
endpoints.result: 15 men after urethroplasty vs 29 after urethrotomy.

limitations: Unblinded surgical comparison with missing symptom outcomes.
Restricted to recurrent bulbar disease; not a comparison for every stricture location or cause.
records.applicability: Urethroplasty offers a durability advantage despite similar short-term symptom improvement.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: ROBUST III · 1 year

source.title: One-Year Results for the ROBUST III Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating the Optilume Drug-Coated Balloon for Anterior Urethral Strictures

records.population: Adult men with recurrent anterior stricture ≤3 cm and ≤12 Fr after ≥2 endoscopic treatments; IPSS ≥11 and Qmax <15 mL/s.

sampleSize.analysis: 22 sites; drug-coated balloon vs standard endoscopic treatment.

records.comparison: Paclitaxel-coated balloon vs dilation/direct-vision internal urethrotomy

endpoints.name: Anatomic success: passage of ≥14 Fr instrument
endpoints.uncertainty: P<.001; confidence interval not reported in inspected abstract.

records.followUp: Primary outcome at 6 months; other outcomes through 1 year
limitations: No urethroplasty comparator; industry-sponsored study.
Short recurrent anterior strictures, predominantly bulbar; not evidence for long, obliterative or all penile strictures.
records.applicability: An option for selected recurrent short bulbar disease; do not infer equivalence to urethroplasty.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: Sildenafil pivotal trials · 1998

source.title: Oral Sildenafil in the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction

records.design: Two sequential double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trials
records.population: Men with erectile dysfunction of organic, psychogenic or mixed causes.

sampleSize.analysis: 532 in a 24-week fixed-dose trial; 329 different men in a 12-week flexible-dose trial. The displayed intercourse outcome belongs to the latter.

endpoints.name: Successful intercourse attempts
endpoints.result: 69% of attempts with sildenafil vs 22% with placebo.
endpoints.uncertainty: P<.001; confidence interval not reported in inspected abstract.

records.followUp: 12 and 24 weeks; a subsequent 32-week extension was open label
limitations: Attempt-level success is not the percentage of men cured.
Selected trial participants; current drug-label contraindications and cardiovascular suitability still apply.
records.applicability: Demonstrates on-treatment efficacy; not proof that spontaneous erectile function is restored.

correction.note: PubMed records an erratum (NEJM 1998;339:59). The corrected indexed abstract was used; the full notice text was not independently assessed.

records.label: REACTT · 2014

source.title: Effects of Tadalafil Treatment on Erectile Function Recovery Following Bilateral Nerve-sparing Radical Prostatectomy: A Randomised Placebo-controlled Study (REACTT)

records.population: Men ≤68 with normal preoperative erectile function undergoing bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy.
records.comparison: Daily or on-demand tadalafil vs placebo

endpoints.name: Unassisted IIEF-EF ≥22 after drug washout
endpoints.uncertainty: Odds ratio vs placebo: daily 1.1 (95% CI 0.6–2.1); on-demand 0.9 (0.5–1.7).

records.followUp: 9 months treatment, 6-week washout, then open-label extension
limitations: Selected nerve-sparing postoperative population; not all causes of ED.
On-treatment benefit must be distinguished from the negative unassisted-recovery endpoint.
records.applicability: PDE5 inhibitors may assist erections after surgery; do not promise improved spontaneous recovery from a rehabilitation schedule.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: ALTAR · 2022

source.title: Alternative to Prophylactic Antibiotics for the Treatment of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections in Women: Multicentre, Open Label, Randomised, Non-inferiority Trial

records.population: Adult women with recurrent UTI for whom prophylaxis was indicated; excluded neurogenic dysfunction and correctable urinary abnormalities.

sampleSize.analysis: 120 randomized per group; modified intention-to-treat primary analysis required ≥6 months follow-up.

records.comparison: Methenamine hippurate vs daily low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis

endpoints.name: Symptomatic antibiotic-treated UTI episodes per person-year
endpoints.uncertainty: Absolute difference 0.49 episodes/year; 90% CI 0.15–0.84; prespecified noninferiority margin 1 episode/year.

records.followUp: 12 months treatment plus 6 months off treatment
limitations: Open label; noninferiority allows some extra infections and is not equivalence.
Does not establish safety in label-contraindicated renal/hepatic disease or benefit from adding vitamin C.
records.applicability: An antibiotic-sparing option after shared decisions; check the drug hub for contraindications and dosing.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.

records.label: MERIT · 2024

source.title: d-Mannose for Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection Among Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial

records.population: Adult women with recurrent UTI at 99 UK primary-care centres.

sampleSize.analysis: 303 assigned d-mannose, 295 placebo; primary outcome available in 294 and 289.

endpoints.name: At least one medically attended clinically suspected UTI
endpoints.uncertainty: Risk difference −5 percentage points; 95% CI −13 to 3; P=.26.

limitations: Primary outcome was clinically suspected, not necessarily culture-confirmed, UTI.
Results do not support routine prophylaxis; absence of statistical significance does not prove a zero effect.
records.applicability: Do not routinely recommend d-mannose for prevention in this population.

correction.note: No linked correction/retraction notice found in the Europe PMC indexed record. This metadata check is not an exhaustive publisher review.
